newsitem.title: INDIA: India deregulates production of electronics goods.
newsitem.headline: India deregulates production of electronics goods.

text.p: The Indian Industry Ministry said on Wednesday that a cabinet committee has ended licencing controls on the production of "entertainment electronics" goods.

It said in a statement that the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs delicensed, or deregulated, production in the sector, which includes manufacture of video cassette recorders, colour televisions, compact disc players and tape recorders.
Currently 15 industries are subject to compulsory licensing under a 1951 law, the ministry said in a statement.
It said entertainment electronics industries had large employment potential, and deregulation would enable entreprenuers to set up units depending on market needs.
It said the Industry Ministry would continue with the policy of deregulation in line with the government's commitment to press ahead with economic liberalisation.
